verses.zh: （大卫的诗，交与伶长。）耶和华啊，求你拯救我脱离凶恶的人，保护我脱离强暴的人！
verses.en: For the music director, a psalm of David.O Lord, rescue me from wicked men.[NOTE:1] Protect me from violent men,[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 140. The psalmist asks God to deliver him from his deadly enemies, calls judgment down upon them, and affirms his confidence in God’s justice.
Heb “from a wicked man.” The Hebrew uses the singular in a representative or collective sense (note the plural verbs in v. 2).

verses.zh: 他们心中图谋奸恶，常常聚集要争战。
verses.en: who plan ways to harm me.[NOTE:1] All day long they stir up conflict.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “a man of violent acts.” The Hebrew uses the singular in a representative or collective sense (note the plural verbs in v. 2).
Heb “they devise wicked [plans] in [their] mind.”

verses.zh: 他们使舌头尖利如蛇，嘴里有虺蛇的毒气。（细拉）
verses.en: Their tongues wound like a serpent;[NOTE:1] a viper’s[NOTE:2] venom is behind[NOTE:3] their lips. (Selah)
notes: Heb “they attack [for] war.” Some revocalize the verb (which is a Qal imperfect from גּוּר, gur, “to attack”) as יְגָרוּ (yegaru), a Piel imperfect from גָרָה (garah, “stir up strife”). This is followed in the present translation.

Heb “they sharpen their tongue like a serpent.” Ps 64:3 reads, “they sharpen their tongues like sword.” Perhaps Ps 140:3 uses a mixed metaphor, the point being that “they sharpen their tongues [like a sword],” as it were, so that when they speak, their words wound like a serpent’s bite. Another option is that the language refers to the pointed or forked nature of a serpent’s tongue, which is viewed metaphorically as “sharpened.”
The Hebrew term is used only here in the OT.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你拯救我脱离恶人的手，保护我脱离强暴的人！他们图谋推我跌倒。
verses.en: O Lord, shelter me from the power[NOTE:1] of the wicked.Protect me from violent men,who plan to knock me over.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “under.”
Heb “hands.”

verses.zh: 骄傲人为我暗设网罗和绳索；他们在路旁铺下网，设下圈套。（细拉）
verses.en: Proud men hide a snare for me;evil men[NOTE:1] spread a net by the path.They set traps for me. (Selah)
notes: Heb “to push down my steps.”

verses.zh: 我曾对耶和华说：你是我的　神。耶和华啊，求你留心听我恳求的声音！
verses.en: I say to the Lord, “You are my God.”O Lord, pay attention to my plea for mercy.

verses.zh: 主―耶和华、我救恩的力量啊，在争战的日子，你遮蔽了我的头。
verses.en: O Sovereign Lord, my strong deliverer,[NOTE:1] you shield[NOTE:2] my head in the day of battle.
notes: Heb “and ropes,” but many prefer to revocalize the noun as a participle (חֹבְלִים, khovelim) from the verb חָבַל (khaval, “act corruptly”).
Heb “the strength of my deliverance.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你不要遂恶人的心愿；不要成就他们的计谋，恐怕他们自高。（细拉）
verses.en: O Lord, do not let the wicked have their way.[NOTE:1] Do not allow their[NOTE:2] plan to succeed when they attack.[NOTE:3] (Selah)
notes: Heb “cover.”
Heb “do not grant the desires of the wicked.”
Heb “his.” The singular is used in a representative sense (see v. 1).

verses.zh: 至于那些昂首围困我的人，愿他们嘴唇的奸恶陷害（原文是遮蔽）自己！
verses.en: As for the heads of those who surround me—may the harm done by[NOTE:1] their lips overwhelm them.
notes: Heb “his plot do not promote, they rise up.” The translation understands the final verb as being an unmarked temporal clause. Another option is to revocalize the verb as a Hiphil and take the verb with the next verse, “those who surround me lift up [their] head,” which could refer to their proud attitude as they anticipate victory (see Ps 27:6).

verses.zh: 愿火炭落在他们身上！愿他们被丢在火中，抛在深坑里，不能再起来。
verses.en: May he rain down[NOTE:1] fiery coals upon them.May he throw them into the fire.From bottomless pits they will not escape.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “harm of their lips.” The genitive here indicates the source or agent of the harm.

The verb form in the Kethib (consonantal Hebrew text) appears to be a Hiphil imperfect from the root מוּט (mut, “to sway”), but the Hiphil occurs only here and in Ps 55:3, where it is preferable to read יַמְטִירוּ (yamtiru, “they rain down”). In Ps 140:10 the form יַמְטֵר (yamter, “let him rain down”) should probably be read.

verses.zh: 说恶言的人在地上必坚立不住；祸患必猎取强暴的人，将他打倒。
verses.en: A slanderer[NOTE:1] will not endure on[NOTE:2] the earth;calamity will hunt down a violent man and strike him down.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “into bottomless pits, they will not arise.” The translation assumes that the preposition ב (bet) has the nuance “from” here. Another option is to connect the line with what precedes, take the final clause as an asyndetic relative clause, and translate, “into bottomless pits [from which] they cannot arise.” The Hebrew noun מַהֲמֹרָה (mahamorah, “bottomless pit”) occurs only here in the OT.
Heb “a man of a tongue.”
Heb “be established in.”

verses.zh: 我知道耶和华必为困苦人伸冤，必为穷乏人辨屈。
verses.en: I know[NOTE:1] that the Lord defends the cause of the oppressedand vindicates the poor.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for blows.” The Hebrew noun מַדְחֵפֹה (madkhefoh, “blow”) occurs only here in the OT.
The translation follows the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss in reading a first person verb form here. The Kethib reads the second person.

verses.zh: 义人必要称赞你的名；正直人必住在你面前。
verses.en: Certainly the godly will give thanks to your name;the morally upright will live in your presence.
